bullets: Dashboard now shows Brews in flight — each brew lists its name, stage (fermenting / conditioning), and day-N-of-M progress so you can see what's actually happening after the brewing day ends.

Get-some-rest now actually ticks the brew forward. Each rest tap increments fermenting and conditioning brews' days_elapsed; when a brew hits its target days, the line turns green and reads ready to bottle (or ready to drink). Bottling itself isn't a real action yet — that lands once the bottling-day flow ships — but at least the path forward is visible instead of looking stuck.
Brewing-day brews don't accrue days because the player is in the active scene during them (per the design's two-clocks rule).

New mini-game: Boil with hops. Set the burner heat (HIGH/MED/LOW), choose whether to watch for hot break and drop hops on schedule, react to a boil-over the way you'd actually react in the kitchen (lower heat / blow / skim / ignore), and remember the flameout. Each choice tweaks the IBU factor, volume loss, and risk deltas.

All seven brewing-day stages except the "heat" warmup now have real mini-games. The full apartment-pale-ale flow plays end-to-end: sanitize → fill kettle → (heat placeholder) → add LME → boil with hops → cool the wort → transfer + pitch. The brew flips to fermenting and you're back on the dashboard.

Boil's UI is form-style for now. The intended end-state is a real-time mini-game with hop-drop prompts, hot-break recognition, and a boil-over reaction window — that lands once the kitchen render-pipeline art is in. The math contract stays the same; only the input affordance changes.

New mini-game: Transfer + pitch yeast (the final brewing-day stage). Pick your pour quality (gentle vs splashy → oxidation risk) and your pitch method (sprinkle on top or rehydrate first → more process XP). Optional toggles for an even sprinkle, stir-before-pitch, and sanitized funnel each tighten care and remove specific risk lines.

New mini-game: Cool the wort. Pick ice bath (slower, lands ~70°F) or top-off cooling (faster, ~80°F, but the cold water is a sanitation gamble unless you boil it first or use bottled). Each path has its own optional sub-actions; the readout previews your projected final temp and care factor as you pick.

New mini-game: Sanitize fermenter & tools. Pick which steps to take — rinse, soap-wash, Star San, drip-dry. The breadth of actions sets your care factor; the strongest action sets the bucket's persistent state (USED → SERVICEABLE → CLEAN → SANITIZED), which carries forward as the next brew's infection-risk baseline.

Star San is shown but greyed out with a (need to buy) tag because the canonical Appendix A starter inventory skips it. Once the phone shop ships you'll be able to buy it during the cold open. Until then the best you can hit is CLEAN.

New mini-game: Pour LME (the Add malt extract stage). The order matters — turn burner OFF, start stirring, THEN pour. Get it wrong and you'll scorch the kettle. Watch for the colored result line for 1.5 seconds before the stage advances so you can see what happened.
Optional toggles (Read recipe aloud, Pre-warm LME tin) raise your care factor without changing the procedure.

Added a dev Reset save button at the bottom of the dashboard. Use it if your save lands in a stuck state — e.g. a brew stranded in fermenting because the bottling flow doesn't ship yet — and you want to drop back to Day 0 with the starter setup. Removed before launch.

Fixed: the day counter resets to Day 0 every relaunch instead of remembering how many days you've slept through. The day clock now rides in the save file and gets restored on load. (Older saves that predate this field default to Day 0 — only the next session forward will start tracking.)

Fixed: Start brewing showed Recipe not unlocked at first launch and only unlocked after a Get-some-rest tap. The bootstrap reseed was running, but the dashboard had already rendered against the pre-reseed state because the state-loaded signal fired too early.
Fixed: tapping Start brewing on the dashboard appeared to do nothing. The brewing-day scene mounts onto a CanvasLayer now, so it actually draws on top of the dashboard.

Fill Kettle is back, rebuilt against the new outcome model. Pick a water source (tap or bottled jug), pick a method (faucet, funnel, 1L pitcher, or marked jug — each with different precision), optionally pour slowly or double-check the volume for a higher care factor.

Pouring rolls a real volume drift against your Process skill, the method's precision, and your care, and writes the result to the brew's outcomes. Lower-skill / lower-precision pours scatter wider; jug-pours land near-exact.
Stages other than Fill kettle still use the placeholder Continue button — they get their real mini-games in upcoming builds.
Dashboard now has a Start brewing button. Tap it to load the brewing-day scene with the Apartment Pale Ale recipe (the only style v1 ships with).

The brewing-day scene shows the seven stages of the brew (Sanitize · Fill kettle · Heat · Add LME · Boil with hops · Cool · Transfer + pitch) in a sidebar; each stage currently advances on a placeholder Continue button until the real mini-games land in the next builds.

Career bootstrap — fresh saves now include the Appendix A starter equipment (stove, stockpot, bucket fermenter, spoon, thermometer, capper, pitcher, funnel) and enough ingredients to brew the starter recipe. Existing in-progress saves migrate forward.
Save format bumped to v2 to carry the bootstrap. Cash, skills, and any in-flight brews are preserved across the migration.
Architecture rebuild against the locked design spec (DESIGN.md Sections 7 + 8). Foundation lands; brewing flow comes back in subsequent commits.
New autoloads: TimeService (the two clocks — day + scene), GameState (the persistent player tree), SaveService (atomic JSON main + JSONL journal).
New scene graph: persistent Dashboard background, ActiveSceneContainer for mini-games, Phone + Modal CanvasLayers above gameplay.
Sim engine pure-data layer: Drift, Grader, RiskProfile, SkillXP, CareFactor, BrewState, CalendarSurface — ready for mini-games to consume.
The previous brew flow + fill-kettle mini-game were proof-of-concept; they're removed and will be reimplemented against the new contract.

Brewing flow! "Start a new brew" on the home screen now walks through nine stages — measure water, mash, boil, cool, pitch, ferment, bottle, condition, taste — with the kettle mini-game for the first one and "Continue" placeholders for the others.
Each completed stage shows its grade in the stage list. Final grade screen with computed OG / IBU / ABV / volume from the recipe target.
Recipe: Basic Pale Ale (target 4.0 L, ~5% ABV, IBU 35). More recipes land later as progression.

Home-screen equipment icons are now all procedural: stove (with burner + red knobs), kettle (side-view), mash paddle, hydrometer (amber wort sample), beer bottle (gold cap + label). Same palette + lighting as the in-game kettle.
Steam rises from the kettle when there's water in it. Soft cream puffs that grow and fade as they drift upward.
Visual polish pass — single global palette + light direction across every procedural-drawn surface, brass faucet (was gray), kettle with proper lit/shadow sides and a counter shadow.
Post-process layer on the kettle mini-game: vignette, warm color grade, soft bloom on bright highlights, subtle film grain.
Replaced the top-down pot icon on the home screen with a side-view procedural kettle that matches the in-game style.

First mini-game: Fill the kettle. Hold POUR to open the faucet, watch the water rise, tap DONE when the level matches the 4.00 L target. Grade is A+ to F based on accuracy; overflowing the kettle ends the round.
Side-view brew kettle drawn procedurally — hammered-metal body, D-handles, rivets, animated water surface with meniscus, splashes where the stream hits the water.
Side gauge with target band so you can see how close you are without watching the readout.
Reachable via the new "Start brewing — fill the kettle" button on the home screen.
Tapping the update notification now installs the new build in-place — no more browser detour.
Home screen now shows a starter brewing kit grid: stove, pot, mash paddle, hydrometer, hops, malt, yeast, and a finished bottle.
Three new sprites: yeast packet, mash paddle, hydrometer.

Fixed the FCM + in-app updater pipeline: a bad type annotation in the export plugin was silently disabling everything in the APK (no notifications, Update button did nothing). Plugin loads cleanly now.
Push notifications: now actually prompts for the Android notification permission on first launch (was silently dropped on Android 13+).
Fixed the build number on the home screen — was always reading 0.
In-app install: tap Update on the home banner and the new build downloads inside the app, then prompts to install — no browser detour.
Push notifications: when a new build ships you'll now get an Android notification, tap it to grab the APK.
Switched the Android build to Godot's gradle pipeline so we can layer in custom Java; CI verifies the APK is still signed with the same key as previous releases.
In-app updater: home screen now shows an Update banner when a newer build is on GitHub.
Tapping Update opens the release page in your browser to download the APK.
First sprite art lands: an amber beer bottle on the home screen.
AI sprite pipeline online — pixel-art SDXL workflow generating equipment + ingredient sprites.
Migrated from Jetpack Compose to Godot 4.3
New project structure: godot/ project + headless screenshot harness + GUT tests
Phase 1 bootstrap: launches to a Hello Homebrewer screen with version + changelog
FCM update push paused until Phase 2 (Android Custom Build template)
